                                                                                                                                                                                                           INTEGRATED TEACHER EDUCATION PROGRAMME (ITEP)
                                                     AT RANGAPARA COLLEGE (AUTONOMOUS)

                                                     Rangapara College (A) is proud to introduce the Integrated Teacher Education Programme (ITEP) – B.A. B.Ed. from the academic session 2025–
                                                26. This four-year integrated course has been approved and recognized by the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) with an intake capacity
                                                of 50 students. Designed in line with the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the ITEP aims to prepare dedicated and competent
                                                educators who are well-equipped with both subject knowledge and pedagogical skills. The course offers a seamless blend of undergraduate education
                                                in Arts with comprehensive training in education, enabling students to graduate with dual degrees: Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) and Bachelor of Education
                                                (B.Ed.). The curriculum is structured to include interdisciplinary studies, inclusive education practices, educational psychology, and hands-on teaching
                                                experience through school internships.




                                                    Rangapara College (A) has appointed a team of qualified and experienced faculty members committed to delivering high-quality teacher
                                                education. The college is also developing dedicated infrastructure, including smart classrooms, a well-equipped education laboratory, and access to
                                                digital learning resources, to support the academic and practical needs of the students. With the introduction of ITEP, Rangapara College (A) reaffirms
                                                its commitment to fostering academic excellence and shaping future educators who can meet the demands of 21st-century classrooms with creativity,
                                                empathy, and professionalism. This programme offers an excellent opportunity for students aspiring to become teachers, providing them with a robust
                                                foundation and a competitive edge in the field of education.

8. Merit List Preparation (Preference-Based System)
The merit list will be prepared based on both applicant preference and academic merit.
Applicants who select the college as their first preference will be given priority over those who
select it as a second or lower preference. For example, if Applicant A secures 90% marks but
gives the college as their 2nd preference and Applicant B secures 80% marks but gives the
college as his 1st preference, then Applicant B will be ranked higher. However, among
applicants with the same preference level, ranking will be determined strictly on the basis of
merit.Moreover, while preparing the category-wise merit list, if a sufficient number of
applicants is not available under a particular preference level, applicants from the next lower
preference level will be considered.

from Preference 2, and 5 from Preference 3 Applicants who have opted for Preference 4, even
if they have higher marks than those in Preferences 1, 2, or 3, will not be considered at this
stage. They will be considered in subsequent merit lists only if seats remain vacant.

9. Subject-wise Merit List Consideration of Subject Preference
Separate merit lists will be prepared for each subject or course offered by the college. The
preference-based system, along with the Government reservation policy, will be applied
individually to each subject. The subject preferences indicated by applicants will be taken into
account while preparing subject-wise merit lists.A candidate’s priority will depend on the
preference assigned to each subject. For example, if an applicant selects Education as his or her
first preference and Political Science as second preference, the applicant will be considered a
first-preference candidate for Education and a second-preference candidate for Political
Science. Within each subject, higher preference candidates will be given priority, and merit
will be applied within the same preference category.

If an applicant takes admission in one subject and later his or her name appears in a subsequent
merit list for another preferred subject, the applicant may withdraw from the previously
admitted subject and take admission in the new subject. Such withdrawal of admission will be
carried out in accordance with Government guidelines and the functioning of the Samarth
portal.
 10. Special Provisions for Specific Subjects
In subjects such as Bodo and Bengali, if applicants from certain reserved categories are not
available, the corresponding seats may be treated as unreserved in accordance with permissible
rules during admission based on the merit list.

In the case of Bengali, if no applicants are available from the ST(P) and ST(H) categories,
those seats shall be treated as unreserved and a preference-based merit list will be prepared
from among the available categories. Similarly, in the case of Bodo, if applicants are available
only from the ST(P) category and not from other reserved categories, the seats shall be treated
as unreserved and a preference-based merit list will be prepared accordingly. However, if
applicants from other reserved categories are available, they shall be considered as per
government reservation norms and separate preference-based merit lists will be prepared for
those categories.

11. Minor and Other Course Selection (SEC, AEC, VAC, MDC)
Seats in Minor subjects are limited. If the seats in a particular subject are exhausted, applicants
will be required to choose from other available subjects at the time of admission. Applicants
must report for admission with the admission confirmation form and clearly indicate their
choices for Minor and other courses such as SEC (Skill Enhancement Course), AEC (Ability
Enhancement Course), VAC (Value Added Course) and MDC (Multidisciplinary Course). In
case the seats in these courses are also filled, applicants must select from the remaining
available options as offered by the college.


12. Subject Change Policy
No request for change of Major subject will be entertained during the admission process from
merit list. Applicants must submit separate applications for different subjects as per
SAMARTH guidelines and each application will be considered independently.


13. Spot Admission
Spot admission, if conducted, will be carried out on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to
the availability of vacant seats. Initially, the Government reservation policy will be followed;
however, after a certain stage, any remaining vacant seats may be treated as unreserved and
filled accordingly. Detailed guidelines regarding spot admission will be issued separately and
published on the college website, if applicable.
 14. Refund Policy
Rangapara College (Autonomous) adheres to the UGC Fee Refund Policy, the details of which
are available on the college website. Applicants are advised to review the policy carefully
before proceeding with admission.


15. Declaration
Students admitted to the First Semester of the Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUGP)
(B.A./B.Sc./B.Com.) under NEP 2020 at Rangapara College may continue their studies up to
the Sixth Semester (Third Year) of the programme. Upon successful completion of the first six
semesters and fulfillment of the prescribed requirements, students shall be awarded a Three-
Year Undergraduate Degree by Gauhati University as per the applicable UGC regulations.
Admission to the First Semester of FYUGP does not automatically confer the right to continue
into the Fourth Year (Honours/Research) of the programme or to secure admission to a Two-
Year Postgraduate Programme. However, students who meet the eligibility criteria prescribed
by the University, UGC and the College may be permitted to pursue the Fourth Year of
FYUGP or enrol in a Two-Year Postgraduate Programme in those departments where such
programmes are offered at Rangapara College.


16. Grievance Redressal for admission
Any grievance regarding admission may be submitted to the Principal of the college. The
grievance will be addressed by the Admission Committee within two days. If the application
requires immediate attention to meet any admission deadline, it will be given priority and
resolved at the earliest.
